title: Utah DWR partners with 17 counties to ban target shooting in wildlife management areas
text:
Because of wildfire risk, the Utah Division of Wildlife Resources is partnering with 17 counties to temporarily ban target shooting with firearms in their wildl
Utah Division of Wildlife Resources said there have been 104 wild animals killed illegally, or poached, since Aug. 1, 2024. Because of wildfire risk, the Utah Division of Wildlife Resources is partnering with 17 counties to temporarily ban target shooting with firearms in their wildlife management areas.
They're partnering with local sheriff's offices to enact the ban, but despite having seen four wildfires in the Saratoga Springs area in June due to target shooting, Utah County is not on the list. 2News reached out to Saratoga Springs to ask them for their thoughts on the ban. While they told us they"Saratoga Springs has experienced six human-caused wildfires since June 1, four of which were started by target shooting.
Given the severe and extreme drought conditions across Utah, we support the state in taking any measures it determines are necessary to reduce the risk of human-caused wildfires and protect lives, property, and natural resources. We encourage anyone planning to target shoot this summer to consider using one of the local indoor shooting ranges or the Utah County public shooting range near Soldier Pass, where they can continue to enjoy the activity in a designated area.
""Typically, we are very supportive of target shooting," said Faith Heaton Jolley, public information officer with the Utah Division of Wildlife Resources. "But just because of the extreme conditions we're seeing this year, we wanted to basically try to prevent any possible wildfire starts. "More than 100 condos, 30 cabins destroyed in Cottonwood Fire at Eagle Point Ski Resort The ban on target shooting with firearms starts July 1st and lasts for the next two weeks.
After that, Utah DWR will re-evaluate conditions. 17 counties with wildlife management areas and their respective sheriff's officers signed on with DWR to approve this ban, but Utah County is not on the list, and Saratoga Springs has seen six wildfires since June 1st — four of which were caused by target shooting, including the Glambert Lane Fire. DWR told 2News only the counties that have those wildlife management areas and whose sheriff's offices gave approvals are on the list.
So, we reached out to the Utah County Sheriff's Office to ask if they had heard from DWR about this, and if so, why did they decide not to sign on?
"We have been in talks with DWR, the State Forestry Office, and BLM negotiating about what would be the best course of action for fire restrictions here in Utah County. This includes target shooting. What we, as the Utah County Sheriff's Office, want is uniformity and consistency. That way the general public can understand what they can and can not do.
Sheriff Smith is waiting to hear back from DWR at this time.
"People in Saratoga Springs had mixed reactions: some did not want to see a ban and wanted people to just use common sense, while others thought it might not be such a bad idea. "I'm kind of more neutral on it, but I guess like if that many other counties are doing it, it's not going to hurt anything to have a ban," said one resident who asked to be kept anonymous.
"Like, two weeks isn't a huge portion of time. I don't think it's really that much of a hindrance on anybody.
" Restricted areas will have signs letting people know, and the Utah Department of Natural Resources Law Enforcement Division will be out patrolling. People violated the ban could be fined up to $1,000. Attorneys for Kouri Richins have asked the court to throw out her convictions and grant her a new trial, arguing she was denied a fair trial.
